question: How will the radius of a nucleus change if its mass number becomes $8$ times its original value? Give reason.

options.A: If $A'=8A$, then $R'=R_0(8A)^{1/3}=2R_0A^{1/3}=2R$. Thus, the radius becomes twice the original radius.
options.B: The radius becomes eight times because $R\propto A$.
options.C: The radius becomes four times because $R\propto A^{1/2}$.
options.D: The radius remains unchanged because it is independent of mass number.
